project.name: AI-Code Accountability Ledger
project.one_line_description: Continuous visibility into which code was AI-generated, how deeply it was reviewed, and where unowned/unexplained business-critical code risk is concentrated.
project.status: pre-implementation, plan freeze pending human approval

requirement_status_legend.confirmed: Explicitly decided in the blueprint and not contested since.
requirement_status_legend.assumption: A reasonable default chosen in the blueprint but not validated against real users/data.
requirement_status_legend.requires_validation: Cannot safely proceed past a certain point without external confirmation (customer, legal, vendor API, pricing).
requirement_status_legend.unknown: Genuinely not knowable yet; must be discovered during build or validation, not assumed.

findings.issue: Backend language (Node/TypeScript vs Python) was left as a team-capability decision in the blueprint, not resolved.
Primary AI provider was not named; blueprint only specifies selection criteria (structured output support, verified data-retention/training terms for source code).
Buyer persona (Engineering leadership vs Security/Compliance) is unresolved and affects Phase 0 validation script design and later feature prioritization order.
No repository currently exists. All file/component names below are logical/proposed, not literal paths, until PHASE-1 initializes the repo.
Free-tier claims for any hosting/DB/AI provider in the blueprint were explicitly marked 'requires verification at build time' and must not be treated as current fact in this plan.
findings.status: carried forward as a standing rule

pre_flight_contradiction_check.conclusion: No hard contradictions found in the source blueprint. Several decisions were deliberately deferred there and must be resolved as explicit gated tasks in this plan rather than assumed now.

roles.human_developer: Owns credentials, accounts, business/legal/compliance decisions, customer validation, architecture approval, risk acceptance, and final sign-off on every phase gate.
roles.planning_and_review_layer: This role (the assistant acting as technical PM/architect/QA/security lead). Maintains architectural consistency, reviews IDE output, updates this plan, detects scope creep and contradictions, tracks unknowns and risks.
roles.ai_coding_ide: Implementation only. Inspects repo before acting, implements only approved scope for the current sub-phase, runs real tests, reports results and assumptions truthfully, halts on architectural conflict.

execution_model.execution_rule: One phase at a time. Within a phase, one sub-phase at a time. No sub-phase begins until the previous sub-phase's completion_criteria are verified, not just claimed.
ai_ide_constraints: Must inspect existing repository state before implementing any task.
Must state intended changes before making them.
Must implement only the approved scope of the current task.
Must run actual tests/commands and report real output, never a claimed result.
Must never delete existing functionality without explicit human approval.
Must never install a new dependency not listed in the task's approved scope without flagging it first.
Must never replace an architecturally-decided technology without explicit approval.
Must never disable, weaken, or bypass a security control to make a test pass.
Must never hardcode secrets, tokens, or credentials anywhere in source.
Must never invent behavior for an external API it has not verified against real documentation or a real response.
Must halt and request clarification immediately if a task conflicts with a previous architectural decision recorded in this plan or the blueprint.
Must report assumptions explicitly rather than silently proceeding on them.
human_developer_required_for: Creating and funding cloud/hosting accounts (Vercel, Render/Railway, Supabase/RDS, etc.)
Creating and funding AI provider accounts and confirming their data-retention/training terms
Legal review of Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, DPA template
Any compliance determination (GDPR posture, SOC 2 timing, EU AI Act applicability)
Approving any architectural change proposed mid-build
Recruiting and conducting Phase 0 customer validation conversations
Final risk acceptance on any unresolved 'requires_validation' item that a phase gate depends on

global_rules: No phase begins until its listed dependencies are marked complete and verified, not just 'appears done'.
No task is marked complete without its Definition of Done being explicitly checked, including tests run and passing.
No AI-derived output is ever persisted or displayed to a user without passing schema validation first, per the blueprint's AI reliability design.

No sensitive data classification introduced in the blueprint's Data Flow section may be violated by any implementation task; any task that would send more than a scoped snippet to an external AI provider is a critical conflict and must halt.
Every database schema change must go through a versioned migration, never a manual/ad hoc change, even in development.
Every external service integration must have its actual current pricing/free-tier terms verified at the time of integration, not assumed from this plan or the earlier blueprint.
Tenant isolation (organization-scoped data access) must be verified by an explicit adversarial test before any phase touching multi-tenant data is considered done.
No phase that touches production infrastructure or real customer data may be executed without the human developer's explicit sign-off at that phase's gate.

phases.name: Specification Freeze and Market Validation
phases.objective: Confirm there is a real, paying market for the product before committing engineering time beyond a manual/concierge prototype, and resolve the buyer-persona ambiguity flagged in pre-flight check PF-3.
phases.business_reason: The blueprint explicitly identified 'willingness to pay for a new category' and 'which persona buys' as unresolved, high-impact unknowns. Building Phases 1-8 before resolving these risks building a technically excellent product nobody purchases.
phases.technical_reason: Determines whether Phase 2's AI-authorship classifier needs to be credible enough for a Security/Compliance buyer (higher bar, audit-grade) or an Engineering-leadership buyer (lower bar, directional insight is enough) - this materially changes acceptance criteria in later phases.
phases.expected_outcome: Either (a) at least 3 organizations expressing real interest, ideally a paid pilot commitment, with a clearly identified buyer persona, or (b) a documented decision to not proceed, or to pivot scope, based on evidence gathered.

external_dependencies: Access to 5-10 candidate companies/repositories for manual analysis, with permission
required_credentials_access: Human developer's existing professional network/outreach channels; no cloud infrastructure required yet

included: Manual/concierge-style repo analysis using existing open-source tools (e.g., git log/blame inspection, manual diff review) performed by hand, not by a built product
Outreach and interviews with candidate buyers
excluded: Any production code, infrastructure, or automated pipeline
affected_users: Human developer only; no end users yet

sub_phases.name: Candidate identification and outreach
sub_phases.objective: Identify and contact 15-20 candidate organizations that plausibly have meaningful AI-coding-tool adoption.

tasks.title: Build candidate list
tasks.objective: Produce a list of 15-20 target companies/contacts across both hypothesized buyer personas (Engineering leadership and Security/Compliance).
tasks.detailed_description: Human developer compiles a list using existing professional network, LinkedIn/X posts about AI-code-risk anxiety (as identified as a live topic in the earlier research), and any warm introductions available. Split the list roughly evenly between the two candidate buyer personas to allow later comparison.
inputs: Human developer's network and public social posts
expected_outputs: A written list of 15-20 named candidates with contact method and persona hypothesis tagged per contact
tasks.implementation_notes: Not an engineering task; owned by human developer.
tasks.validation: List reviewed for persona balance and realistic reachability before outreach begins.
failure_cases: Fewer than 10 reachable candidates found -> escalate to broaden search criteria before proceeding
tasks.security_considerations: None at this stage.
definition_of_done: List of >=15 candidates exists with contact method and persona tag for each

tasks.title: Send outreach and schedule conversations
tasks.objective: Get commitments to review a manual finding or take a short call from at least 8-10 of the candidates.
tasks.detailed_description: Outreach message references the specific, evidenced problem (AI-authored, under-reviewed, business-critical code) rather than a generic pitch, per the earlier research framing.
expected_outputs: At least 8 scheduled conversations or agreed manual-review engagements
tasks.implementation_notes: Human developer task.
tasks.validation: Count of scheduled engagements tracked against the 8-10 target.
failure_cases: Low response rate (<20%) is itself a signal worth recording, not just a logistics failure - feed into PHASE-0 conclusion
tasks.security_considerations: None.
definition_of_done: >=8 scheduled conversations or manual-review engagements confirmed

sub_phases.testing_strategy: not_applicable
validation_steps: Response rate and engagement count reviewed against thresholds
completion_criteria: >=8 confirmed conversations/engagements
sub_phases.rollback_considerations: not_applicable - no system changes made in this sub-phase
risks: Low response rate delays the entire project start

sub_phases.name: Manual analysis and evidence gathering
sub_phases.objective: For each engaged candidate, manually produce the core insight (AI-authored, low-review-depth, business-critical code heatmap) using existing tools, and gauge reaction.

tasks.title: Run manual repo analysis per candidate
tasks.objective: Produce a one-page finding summary per candidate repo using git history inspection and manual judgment, without building any product.
tasks.detailed_description: Uses git blame/log and manual review to approximate what the future Analysis Engine (blueprint Section 8) would compute: rough AI-authorship signal (where determinable, e.g. commit messages, tool metadata if visible), review time proxy (PR open-to-merge time, comment count), and a manually-applied criticality judgment (auth/payments/data-access paths).
expected_outputs: One-page finding summary per candidate, following the blueprint's Layer 1/2 simple-explanation format
tasks.implementation_notes: This directly tests whether the core value proposition is producible and credible even manually - a precursor validation of the single largest technical risk identified in the blueprint (AI-authorship signal reliability).
tasks.validation: Each summary reviewed by the human developer for internal credibility before being shown to the candidate.
failure_cases: Manual AI-authorship signal is too unreliable/ambiguous even by hand -> this is a critical finding that must feed directly into PHASE-2 risk planning, not be discarded
tasks.security_considerations: Handle each candidate's code with the same care implied by the blueprint's data-handling principles even though no product exists yet - do not retain repository contents beyond what is needed for the one-page summary, and do not share one candidate's data with another.
definition_of_done: One-page summary produced and internally reviewed for each engaged candidate

tasks.title: Present findings and record reaction
tasks.objective: Share the manual finding with each candidate and record their reaction against the blueprint's 'strong reaction' vs 'weak reaction' test.
tasks.detailed_description: Track explicitly: did they ask 'can you run this on our whole codebase', did they ask about pricing, did they offer to pay for a pilot, or was the reaction lukewarm.
expected_outputs: A structured log of reaction per candidate, tagged strong/weak, with persona noted
tasks.implementation_notes: This is the core data PHASE-0 exists to produce.
tasks.validation: Reviewed against the phase's completion_criteria.
failure_cases: Reaction is weak across the board -> triggers the phase's explicit 'do not proceed as currently scoped' contingency
tasks.security_considerations: Confirm no NDA or confidentiality issue prevents sharing findings back to the candidate in the format chosen.
definition_of_done: Reaction log complete for all engaged candidates

sub_phases.testing_strategy: not_applicable
security_checks: Manual data-handling discipline confirmed (no cross-candidate data mixing, no unnecessary retention)
validation_steps: Reaction log reviewed against strong/weak reaction criteria from the blueprint's customer-reaction test
completion_criteria: Reaction log complete for at least 8 candidates
sub_phases.rollback_considerations: not_applicable
risks: Manual analysis proves the authorship signal is unreliable even by hand - this is a valid and important outcome, not a failure of the phase itself

sub_phases.name: Go/no-go decision and specification freeze
sub_phases.objective: Make an explicit, evidence-based decision to proceed, pivot, or stop, and freeze the product specification for Phase 1.

tasks.title: Synthesize validation findings into a go/no-go decision
tasks.objective: Produce a written decision record answering: is there a real buyer, which persona, and did >=3 candidates express strong interest (ideally with a pilot commitment).
tasks.detailed_description: This decision record becomes part of the frozen specification and directly resolves pre-flight items PF-2 (buyer persona) for downstream phases.
expected_outputs: Decision record: proceed / pivot / stop, with buyer persona resolved if proceeding
tasks.implementation_notes: Owned jointly - human developer decides, planning layer documents the decision's implications for the rest of this plan.
tasks.validation: Decision record reviewed against the >=3-strong-reaction threshold defined in the phase objective.
failure_cases: Fewer than 3 strong reactions -> default outcome is 'do not proceed to Phase 1 as currently scoped'; escalate to human developer for an explicit override decision if they choose to proceed anyway, recorded as an accepted risk
tasks.security_considerations: Not applicable.
definition_of_done: Written decision record exists and is approved by the human developer

sub_phases.testing_strategy: not_applicable
completion_criteria: Signed decision record with explicit proceed/pivot/stop outcome
sub_phases.rollback_considerations: not_applicable
risks: Proceeding despite weak signal purely due to sunk-cost or enthusiasm - flagged explicitly for the human developer to consciously accept or reject

phase_validation.method: Review of the decision record against the >=3-strong-reaction threshold and explicit buyer-persona resolution.
phase_validation.gate: Product Gate (partial) - confirms there is a product worth building before Architecture Gate work begins in Phase 1.

definition_of_done: Decision record exists with explicit proceed/pivot/stop outcome
If proceeding: buyer persona explicitly resolved (Engineering leadership vs Security/Compliance vs both)
If proceeding: at least one candidate has agreed to be a Phase 6 beta participant

phases.name: Repository Initialization and Architecture Foundation
phases.objective: Stand up the repository, development environment, and the skeleton of the modular monolith architecture defined in the blueprint, with no product logic yet.
phases.business_reason: Nothing can be built without a consistent, reviewable foundation; rework here is the most expensive rework possible later.
phases.technical_reason: Establishes the org/repo/user data model, auth scaffold, and service boundaries (Ingestion, Analysis Engine, AI Orchestration, Reporting, Notification) as separate logical modules within one deployable unit, per blueprint Section 8, so later phases have a stable place to add code.
phases.expected_outcome: A running, empty-but-structured application: a developer can sign in via GitHub OAuth and see an empty dashboard, with CI passing on a trivial change.

prerequisite_tasks: PF-2 (AI provider) does not block this phase but should be scheduled for resolution before PHASE-2 begins
required_credentials_access: Human developer must create: GitHub OAuth App client ID/secret, hosting provider account, database provider account, and provide these as environment secrets - never committed to source

included: Basic CI pipeline (lint, type check, test run)
Database connection and initial migration tooling setup
Auth scaffold (GitHub OAuth login only, no authorization logic yet)
affected_users: Human developer and IDE only; no end users

sub_phases.name: Backend language and framework decision execution
sub_phases.objective: Resolve pre-flight item PF-1 and initialize the chosen backend stack.

tasks.title: Human decision: backend language
tasks.objective: Human developer explicitly chooses Node.js/TypeScript or Python for the backend, based on actual team capability, resolving PF-1.
tasks.detailed_description: This is a human decision, not an IDE or planning-layer decision, because the blueprint explicitly deferred it to team capability, which only the human developer can assess.
expected_outputs: Recorded decision: language and primary framework
tasks.implementation_notes: Recorded in this plan's cross_phase_requirements once made.
tasks.validation: Decision recorded and referenced by all subsequent backend tasks.
failure_cases: Decision left unmade -> blocks all of PHASE-1.2 onward
tasks.security_considerations: Not applicable.
definition_of_done: Backend language/framework decision recorded

tasks.title: Initialize repository structure
tasks.objective: Create the repository with a logical module layout matching the blueprint's service boundaries.
tasks.detailed_description: Create top-level structure separating: frontend application, backend application (with internal modules for Auth, Ingestion, Analysis Engine, AI Orchestration, Reporting, Notification per blueprint Section 8), shared type/schema definitions, and infrastructure/config. Exact directory names are logical proposals for the IDE to confirm against actual framework conventions (e.g., Next.js app-router conventions), not fixed in advance.
inputs: Chosen framework's standard project scaffolding tools
expected_outputs: Initialized repository with committed scaffold, README stub, .gitignore, license/ownership file as appropriate
tasks.implementation_notes: IDE must use the framework's official scaffolding tool rather than hand-rolling boilerplate, and must report the exact tool/version used.
tasks.validation: Repository builds and runs locally with a placeholder homepage.
failure_cases: Scaffold tool requires a dependency/version not available in the environment -> report and request human decision, do not silently substitute
security_considerations: Ensure .gitignore excludes any env/secret file patterns from the very first commit
tasks.testing_requirements: Verify the app starts locally without error.
definition_of_done: Repository exists, builds, and runs a placeholder page locally

sub_phases.testing_strategy: Local build/run smoke test only at this stage.
security_checks: .gitignore correctly excludes secrets/env files
validation_steps: Local run confirmed by IDE and spot-checked by human developer
completion_criteria: Repository builds and runs locally
sub_phases.rollback_considerations: Trivial - no persistent data yet; repository can be re-initialized if structure proves wrong.
risks: Wrong initial structure causes rework later if service boundaries are not respected - mitigated by explicit module layout matching blueprint Section 8

sub_phases.name: CI pipeline and code quality baseline
sub_phases.objective: Establish automated lint, type-check, and test execution on every change, before any product logic exists.

tasks.title: Configure linting and formatting
tasks.objective: Enforce a consistent code style automatically.
tasks.detailed_description: Configure the standard linter/formatter for the chosen language (per blueprint Section 12's CI/CD mention), applied to both frontend and backend.
expected_outputs: Lint/format configuration committed, passing on the current scaffold
tasks.implementation_notes: Use widely-adopted, framework-recommended tools rather than an unusual/unverified choice.
tasks.validation: Lint command runs and passes on current codebase.
failure_cases: Conflicting rules between frontend/backend tooling -> resolve by scoping configs per package/directory
tasks.security_considerations: Not applicable.
tasks.testing_requirements: Lint passes with zero errors on initial scaffold.
definition_of_done: Lint/format commands exist and pass

tasks.title: Configure CI pipeline
tasks.objective: Run lint, type-check, and test commands automatically on every push/PR.
tasks.detailed_description: Use GitHub Actions per blueprint Section 12. Pipeline must fail the build if any check fails - no soft-fail/allow-failure steps for these core checks.
expected_outputs: CI workflow file committed and passing on the current scaffold
tasks.implementation_notes: IDE must verify the CI run actually executes and passes remotely, not just locally, before marking this done.
tasks.validation: A test PR/commit triggers CI and shows a passing status.
failure_cases: CI environment lacks a dependency present locally -> must be fixed in CI config, not worked around by skipping the check
tasks.security_considerations: CI secrets (if any needed even at this stage) must use the CI provider's secret store, never committed values.
tasks.testing_requirements: At least one placeholder test exists and runs in CI.
definition_of_done: CI pipeline exists, runs on push, and passes

sub_phases.testing_strategy: CI itself is the validation mechanism from this point forward.
security_checks: No secrets present in CI configuration files
validation_steps: Observed passing CI run on a real commit
completion_criteria: CI passes on current scaffold
sub_phases.rollback_considerations: Low risk - CI config changes are easily reverted.
risks: Overly strict CI rules block early development velocity - mitigated by keeping the baseline minimal (lint, type-check, placeholder test) and expanding as real code is added

sub_phases.name: Database provisioning and migration tooling
sub_phases.objective: Provision the development database and establish a controlled migration workflow before any schema is defined.

tasks.title: Human task: provision managed Postgres (dev)
tasks.objective: Create a development Postgres instance with the chosen managed provider.
tasks.detailed_description: Per blueprint Section 12, using Supabase or an equivalent managed provider. Human developer must verify current free-tier terms at the time of signup rather than trusting the blueprint's prior description, per global_rules.
expected_outputs: Database connection string, stored as a secret, not committed
tasks.implementation_notes: Human developer task; IDE only consumes the resulting connection string via environment variable.
tasks.validation: Connection verified from a local script.
failure_cases: Free-tier limits are lower than expected -> record as a cost_control note, not a blocker for dev
tasks.security_considerations: Connection string treated as a secret from the moment it exists.
definition_of_done: Working dev database connection available as an environment variable

tasks.title: Establish migration tooling
tasks.objective: Set up a versioned migration system so all future schema changes are tracked, reviewable, and reversible.
tasks.detailed_description: Use the migration tool native to the chosen backend framework/ORM. No manual schema edits permitted from this point forward, per global_rules.
expected_outputs: Migration tooling configured, with an initial empty migration applied successfully
tasks.implementation_notes: IDE must confirm migrations run cleanly against a fresh database, and that a rollback command exists and is tested.
tasks.validation: Migration up and down both verified to work on a disposable test database.
failure_cases: Migration tool incompatible with chosen ORM -> flag and request human decision on ORM choice
tasks.security_considerations: Row-Level Security (RLS) capability confirmed available on the chosen Postgres provider, since it is required by blueprint Section 10, even though RLS policies themselves are not written until PHASE-4.
tasks.testing_requirements: Migration up/down tested against a disposable database instance.
definition_of_done: Migration tooling functional, initial empty migration applied and reversible

sub_phases.testing_strategy: Migration up/down tested on a disposable database.
security_checks: Connection string never committed to source
RLS capability confirmed available on chosen provider
validation_steps: Successful migration up and down observed
completion_criteria: Migration tooling works, RLS capability confirmed
sub_phases.rollback_considerations: Migrations are the rollback mechanism itself; verified bidirectionally before proceeding.
risks: Chosen Postgres provider does not support RLS as assumed in the blueprint -> this would be a genuine architectural conflict requiring escalation to the human developer, not a silent workaround

sub_phases.name: Authentication scaffold (login only, no authorization yet)
sub_phases.objective: Allow a user to sign in via GitHub OAuth, establishing the identity foundation the rest of the system depends on.

tasks.title: Human task: register GitHub OAuth App
tasks.objective: Create the OAuth application credentials required for login.
tasks.detailed_description: Per blueprint Section 17, GitHub OAuth is the primary authentication mechanism since repository access is required regardless.
expected_outputs: OAuth client ID and secret, stored as environment secrets
tasks.implementation_notes: Human developer task.
tasks.validation: Credentials present as environment variables, never committed.
failure_cases: Callback URL misconfigured for dev environment -> update OAuth App settings, not application code, to fix
tasks.security_considerations: Client secret treated as a secret from creation.
definition_of_done: OAuth App credentials available as environment variables

tasks.title: Implement GitHub OAuth login flow
tasks.objective: Implement sign-in via GitHub OAuth with secure session issuance, per blueprint Sections 10 and 17.
tasks.detailed_description: On successful OAuth callback: verify the OAuth state parameter to prevent CSRF on the auth flow, create or update a User record, issue a short-lived session token stored in an httpOnly secure cookie, and redirect to the (currently empty) dashboard. No Organization/Membership logic yet - that is PHASE-1.5.
expected_outputs: Working login flow: unauthenticated user is redirected to GitHub, returns authenticated, session cookie set
tasks.implementation_notes: Session tokens must be short-lived with a refresh mechanism per blueprint Section 10 - do not implement long-lived tokens as a shortcut.
tasks.validation: Manual login flow tested end-to-end in dev; session cookie inspected to confirm httpOnly and secure flags.
failure_cases: OAuth state mismatch -> reject and show a clear error, never silently proceed
GitHub API unavailable -> show a clear error state, per blueprint Section 14 failure-handling pattern applied even at this early stage
security_considerations: OAuth CSRF protection via state parameter is mandatory, not optional
Session cookie must be httpOnly, secure, and appropriately scoped
testing_requirements: Integration test covering successful login
Integration test covering OAuth state-mismatch rejection
Integration test covering GitHub API failure during callback
definition_of_done: Login flow works end-to-end in dev with passing tests for success and both failure cases listed

sub_phases.testing_strategy: Integration tests for success and named failure cases; manual verification of cookie security flags.
security_checks: OAuth CSRF protection verified
Session cookie flags verified
No secrets committed
validation_steps: Manual end-to-end login test in dev environment
completion_criteria: A real GitHub account can log in and reach an authenticated (empty) dashboard route
sub_phases.rollback_considerations: Auth is foundational; any later change to the auth model requires an explicit migration and is treated as a higher-risk change in later phases.
risks: Session/cookie misconfiguration is a common and serious mistake - explicitly tested rather than assumed correct

sub_phases.name: Organization and Membership data model
sub_phases.objective: Introduce the tenant boundary (Organization) and the User-to-Organization relationship (Membership), establishing the root of the multi-tenant model before any product data exists.

tasks.title: Implement Organization and Membership schema
tasks.objective: Create the Organization and Membership entities per blueprint Section 16, with Role as an enum on Membership.
tasks.detailed_description: On first login, if the user has no Organization, prompt creation of one (single-organization-per-signup default for V1; the blueprint does not specify multi-org support as a V1 requirement, so this is treated as out of scope unless later flagged otherwise).
expected_outputs: Organization and Membership tables via migration
First-login organization-creation flow
tasks.implementation_notes: Role enum values at minimum: org_admin, team_lead, developer, read_only, matching blueprint Section 2 personas A-F mapped to concrete roles.
tasks.validation: New user login creates an Organization and Membership record correctly; existing user login does not duplicate.
failure_cases: Race condition on simultaneous first-login organization creation -> must be handled with a database-level uniqueness constraint, not application-only logic
security_considerations: Organization ID becomes the tenant boundary referenced by every future RLS policy - correctness here is foundational to Section 10's entire tenant-isolation model
testing_requirements: Unit test for role enum constraints
Integration test for first-login organization creation
Integration test for the race-condition case
definition_of_done: Organization/Membership schema exists, first-login flow works, race condition test passes

sub_phases.testing_strategy: Unit and integration tests as listed in T-1.5.1.
security_checks: Organization ID confirmed as the consistent tenant-scoping key going forward
completion_criteria: A logged-in user has exactly one Organization and Membership record with a valid role
sub_phases.rollback_considerations: Schema is new and additive; low risk at this stage since no dependent product data exists yet.
risks: Getting the tenant model wrong here compounds into every later phase - deliberately reviewed carefully before proceeding, per global_rules on RLS verification

phase_validation.method: Architecture Gate review: confirm the repository structure matches blueprint Section 8's service boundaries, auth and tenant model are correctly foundational, CI is green.

definition_of_done: Repository initialized with logical module boundaries matching the blueprint
CI pipeline green on lint, type-check, and test execution
Working GitHub OAuth login with secure session handling
Organization/Membership tenant model established and tested
No product/analysis logic yet - correctly out of scope for this phase

phases.name: Repository Integration and Ingestion Pipeline
phases.objective: Allow an Organization to connect a real GitHub repository and reliably ingest commit/PR metadata, with no analysis yet.
phases.business_reason: This is the data foundation every other feature depends on; it must be reliable before analysis logic is trusted.
phases.technical_reason: Implements the Ingestion Service and Repository/Commit/PullRequest entities from blueprint Sections 8 and 16, including webhook handling and the initial backfill job pattern from blueprint Section 7 step 3.
phases.expected_outcome: A connected repository's commit/PR history (bounded lookback window) is visible as raw data in the dashboard, and new commits/PRs arrive automatically via webhook.

external_dependencies: GitHub API access via the OAuth token already obtained in PHASE-1
A real test repository with realistic history for validation
required_credentials_access: GitHub App or OAuth scope sufficient for repo read + webhook management - human developer must confirm exact scopes against current GitHub documentation, this is not assumed

included: Repo, Commit, PullRequest entities and migrations
Background job queue setup (Postgres-backed, per blueprint Section 8)
Raw data display in a minimal repo view
excluded: Any Finding entity - that begins in PHASE-3

sub_phases.name: Repository connection flow
sub_phases.objective: Let an Org Admin select and connect a GitHub repository the OAuth-authenticated user has access to.

tasks.title: Verify and finalize required GitHub OAuth/App scopes
tasks.objective: Confirm, against current GitHub documentation at implementation time, exactly which scopes are required for repo read access and webhook management, resolving what was left as 'requires verification' in the blueprint.
tasks.detailed_description: This must be checked live, not assumed from prior knowledge, since GitHub API scope requirements can change.
expected_outputs: Documented, confirmed scope list
tasks.implementation_notes: IDE must fetch/verify current documentation rather than relying on training data, and report the source checked.
tasks.validation: Scopes tested against a real repository connection in dev.
failure_cases: Required scope differs from what PHASE-1's OAuth App was registered with -> requires human developer to update the OAuth App configuration
tasks.security_considerations: Request the minimum necessary scope, not broad/unnecessary access, per least-privilege principle.
definition_of_done: Confirmed scope list documented and OAuth App configured accordingly

tasks.title: Implement repository picker and connection
tasks.objective: Let the Org Admin see a list of repos accessible to their GitHub account and select one or more to connect.
tasks.detailed_description: Store the connection as a Repository record scoped to the Organization; store integration credentials reference per blueprint Section 16's Integration entity, pointing to a secrets store, not storing raw tokens in the Repository table directly.
inputs: GitHub API repo list response for the authenticated user
expected_outputs: Repository entity created on connection
Repository visible in a minimal repo list UI
tasks.implementation_notes: Must respect GitHub API rate limits per blueprint Section 8 - implement basic backoff even at this stage rather than deferring it.
tasks.validation: Connecting a real test repository succeeds and is visible in the UI.
failure_cases: User has no accessible repos -> clear empty state, not an error
GitHub API rate-limited during list fetch -> graceful retry/backoff, visible loading state
security_considerations: Repository access strictly scoped to the connecting Organization (tenant isolation)
Integration credentials never exposed to the frontend
testing_requirements: Integration test for successful connection
Integration test for empty-repo-list case
Integration test for rate-limit handling
definition_of_done: A real repository can be connected end-to-end and appears correctly scoped to its Organization

sub_phases.testing_strategy: Integration tests for connection success, empty state, and rate-limit handling.
security_checks: Tenant scoping of Repository records verified
Credentials never exposed client-side
validation_steps: Manual connection of a real test repo
completion_criteria: Repository connection flow works end-to-end for a real repo
sub_phases.rollback_considerations: Disconnecting a repo must be a supported, tested action before this sub-phase is considered fully done in later hardening, but a bare disconnect capability should exist even now to avoid orphaned test data.
risks: GitHub API scope/rate-limit specifics differ from documentation at build time - mitigated by verifying live rather than assuming

sub_phases.name: Webhook receiver and signature verification
sub_phases.objective: Receive real-time push/PR events from GitHub reliably and securely.

tasks.title: Implement webhook endpoint with signature verification
tasks.objective: Accept GitHub webhook deliveries, verify their HMAC signature, and reject anything unsigned or invalid, per blueprint Section 10.
tasks.detailed_description: Endpoint is unauthenticated by user session (webhooks are server-to-server) but must verify the GitHub webhook secret signature on every request before processing.
inputs: GitHub webhook payload and signature header
expected_outputs: Verified events stored/queued for processing; invalid signatures rejected with logging
tasks.implementation_notes: Webhook secret stored via the secrets mechanism established in PHASE-1, never hardcoded.
tasks.validation: Test with both a validly signed and an intentionally invalid payload; invalid must be rejected.
failure_cases: Missing signature header -> reject
Signature mismatch -> reject and log as a security event per blueprint Section 21
security_considerations: This is the primary external-facing security boundary from GitHub into the system - must be tested adversarially, not just happy-path
testing_requirements: Test valid signature accepted
Test invalid/missing signature rejected
Test replay of the same delivery ID is handled idempotently (ties into T-2.2.2)
definition_of_done: Webhook endpoint verified secure against invalid/missing signatures with passing tests

tasks.title: Implement idempotent event processing
tasks.objective: Ensure duplicate webhook deliveries (GitHub may redeliver) do not create duplicate data.
tasks.detailed_description: Use GitHub's delivery ID as an idempotency key per blueprint Section 14's explicit failure-handling requirement for duplicate requests.
expected_outputs: Duplicate deliveries recognized and skipped without side effects
tasks.implementation_notes: Store processed delivery IDs with a uniqueness constraint at the database level, not just in-memory.
tasks.validation: Sending the same payload/delivery ID twice results in only one processed effect.
failure_cases: Delivery ID collision across different repos (should not happen per GitHub's design, but verify) -> scope idempotency key by repo/org as well if needed
tasks.security_considerations: Not applicable beyond what T-2.2.1 covers.
testing_requirements: Test duplicate delivery is a no-op on the second attempt
definition_of_done: Duplicate webhook delivery test passes

sub_phases.testing_strategy: Adversarial security tests (invalid signature) plus idempotency tests.
security_checks: HMAC signature verification confirmed
Invalid/missing signature rejected and logged
validation_steps: All listed tests passing in CI
completion_criteria: Webhook endpoint secure and idempotent, verified by tests
sub_phases.rollback_considerations: Low risk - stateless endpoint logic, easily reverted.
risks: An unverified webhook endpoint would be a critical, exploitable vulnerability - explicitly why this sub-phase exists as its own gated unit rather than being bundled loosely into ingestion

sub_phases.name: Background job queue and bounded backfill
sub_phases.objective: Process the initial historical ingestion asynchronously and resumably, per blueprint Sections 7 and 14.

tasks.title: Set up Postgres-backed job queue
tasks.objective: Establish the background job infrastructure per blueprint Section 8's explicit choice to avoid adding Redis prematurely.
tasks.detailed_description: Use a Postgres-backed job queue library appropriate to the chosen backend language, confirmed compatible at implementation time.
expected_outputs: Working job queue capable of enqueueing, processing, and retrying a job
tasks.implementation_notes: IDE must verify current compatibility/maintenance status of the chosen library before adopting it, not assume it from training data.
tasks.validation: A trivial test job enqueues, processes, and completes correctly, including a forced-failure retry test.
failure_cases: Library incompatible with chosen ORM/DB version -> flag and request human decision on alternative
tasks.security_considerations: Not applicable at this stage.
testing_requirements: Test job success path
Test job retry on failure
Test job progress tracking
definition_of_done: Job queue functional with passing tests for success, retry, and progress tracking

tasks.title: Implement bounded-lookback backfill job
tasks.objective: On repository connection, ingest a configurable, bounded window of historical commit/PR data (blueprint suggests 6-12 months as a default, configurable) as a resumable background job.
tasks.detailed_description: Job must be chunked (per-page or per-batch of commits) and resumable if interrupted, per blueprint Section 14's explicit 'partial processing' failure case. Progress must be visible to the user, per blueprint Section 3's loading-state requirement, not a silent spinner.
expected_outputs: Commit and PullRequest records populated for the connected repo, with visible progress during backfill
tasks.implementation_notes: Respect GitHub API rate limits with real backoff, not a fixed sleep - verify current rate-limit response headers/behavior against live GitHub API documentation.
tasks.validation: Backfill of a real test repository completes correctly; interrupting and resuming the job does not duplicate or lose data.
failure_cases: Very large repository causes excessive backfill time -> chunking and progress visibility are the mitigation, not a hard timeout that silently fails
Rate limit hit mid-backfill -> job pauses and resumes automatically, visible to the user as 'processing, resuming shortly' not an error
tasks.security_considerations: Ingested commit/PR metadata is scoped strictly to the connecting Organization; no cross-tenant leakage possible given the Organization-scoped Repository foreign key established in PHASE-1.5/PHASE-2.1.
testing_requirements: Integration test for full backfill completion on a small test repo
Integration test for interrupt-and-resume
Integration test for rate-limit-triggered pause/resume
definition_of_done: Backfill works end-to-end on a real repository, is resumable, and shows real progress in the UI

expected_artifacts: Commit/PullRequest schema and populated data from a real backfill
sub_phases.testing_strategy: Integration tests covering completion, interruption/resume, and rate-limit handling.
security_checks: Tenant scoping of ingested data verified
validation_steps: Real backfill run against a test repository observed end-to-end
completion_criteria: A real repository's bounded history is fully and correctly ingested, resumably
sub_phases.rollback_considerations: Backfill can be safely re-run; idempotency at the data level (unique constraint on commit SHA per repo) prevents duplication on re-run.
risks: This sub-phase directly tests infrastructure that PHASE-2's entire value depends on - treated as high-scrutiny, not routine

sub_phases.name: Minimal raw-data repo view
sub_phases.objective: Make ingested data visible to users, closing the loop for this phase without any analysis logic yet.

tasks.title: Build minimal repo detail page showing raw ingested commits/PRs
tasks.objective: Provide a basic, functional view so the ingestion pipeline's output is verifiable by a human, not just by tests.
tasks.detailed_description: This is intentionally minimal - a list of ingested commits/PRs with basic metadata (author, timestamp, review time if available). No progressive-disclosure Finding UI yet; that begins in PHASE-4.
expected_outputs: A working repo detail page listing ingested data
tasks.implementation_notes: Follow the loading/empty/error state requirements from blueprint Section 3 even at this minimal stage, since this establishes the pattern for later, more complex pages.
tasks.validation: Manual review confirms the displayed data matches what is actually in the database for a real connected repo.
failure_cases: No data yet (backfill in progress) -> correct loading/progress state, not an empty-looking blank page
tasks.security_considerations: Page only shows data for repos the current user's Organization has access to - verified, not assumed.
testing_requirements: Integration test confirming a user cannot view another Organization's repo data (tenant isolation adversarial test, per global_rules)
definition_of_done: Repo detail page correctly and securely displays ingested data

sub_phases.testing_strategy: Manual verification plus an explicit adversarial tenant-isolation test.
security_checks: Tenant isolation adversarial test passing - this is the first mandatory instance of the global_rules requirement
completion_criteria: Repo detail page accurately and securely reflects ingested data
sub_phases.rollback_considerations: Low risk, UI-only.
risks: This is the first point where a real tenant-isolation bug could be caught or missed - treated with the seriousness global_rules assigns it

phase_validation.method: Manual verification of a real repository's ingestion end to end, plus adversarial tenant-isolation test suite passing.
phase_validation.gate: Architecture Gate (extended) and first instance of Security Gate (partial - webhook and tenant isolation only; full Security Gate is PHASE-6).

definition_of_done: A real GitHub repository can be connected, backfilled (bounded window), and kept in sync via webhook
Webhook endpoint verified secure against invalid signatures and duplicate delivery
Tenant isolation verified via an explicit adversarial test
No analysis/AI logic yet - correctly deferred to PHASE-3

phases.name: Deterministic Analysis Engine
phases.objective: Implement review-depth scoring and criticality tagging - the non-AI half of the Analysis Engine - producing the first real Finding records.
phases.business_reason: Deterministic analysis is lower-risk and faster to validate than the AI-authorship classifier, and per blueprint Section 8/24 build order, should be built before AI analysis to establish the Finding data model and UI against reliable, explainable data first.
phases.technical_reason: Implements the Finding entity and the rule-based portions of the Analysis Engine service from blueprint Sections 8 and 16, without yet touching the highest-risk unknown (AI-authorship detection, PF handled in PHASE-4).
phases.expected_outcome: Every ingested PR produces a Finding with a review-depth score and a criticality tag, correctly and explainably, with no AI involved yet.

included: Criticality policy configuration and tagging logic (deterministic)
affected_users: any Member (Findings exist but full UI is PHASE-5, so this phase's UI is minimal/internal-facing)

sub_phases.name: Criticality policy configuration
sub_phases.objective: Let an Org Admin define what counts as 'critical' code, per blueprint Section 5's explicit requirement that this be configurable, not fixed.

tasks.title: Implement CriticalityPolicy entity and default rule set
tasks.objective: Store org- or repo-level path/keyword rules (e.g., paths containing 'auth', 'payment', 'billing') with sensible pre-filled defaults per blueprint Section 3's onboarding wizard requirement.
tasks.detailed_description: Defaults should be a reasonable starting point but must be explicitly editable - do not hardcode them as unchangeable, since the blueprint Section 24 critical unknowns flags that real default rules should come from Phase 0 customer input, not be invented internally. Use whatever was learned in PHASE-0 if applicable; otherwise use clearly-labeled placeholder defaults pending real customer validation.
inputs: PHASE-0 findings if available, otherwise a documented placeholder default set
expected_outputs: CriticalityPolicy table and CRUD API
Basic policy configuration UI
tasks.implementation_notes: Policy rules should support both org-wide defaults and repo-level overrides, per blueprint Section 3's settings page description.
tasks.validation: Creating, editing, and deleting a policy rule works and is correctly scoped to the Organization.
failure_cases: Conflicting org-level and repo-level rules -> repo-level explicitly overrides org-level, documented behavior, not undefined
tasks.security_considerations: Only Org Admin role can modify policy, per the RBAC roles established in PHASE-1.5 - authorization check required, not just UI-level hiding of the control.
testing_requirements: Unit test for rule matching logic
Integration test for CRUD operations with role-based authorization enforcement
Test that a non-admin role cannot modify policy
definition_of_done: Policy CRUD works, correctly scoped and authorized

sub_phases.testing_strategy: Unit tests for matching logic; integration tests for CRUD and authorization.
security_checks: Role-based authorization enforced server-side, not just hidden client-side
completion_criteria: Org Admin can configure criticality rules; non-admins cannot
sub_phases.rollback_considerations: Low risk, additive schema.
risks: Placeholder default rules may be poorly calibrated - explicitly flagged as needing real customer input, not treated as final

sub_phases.name: Review-depth scoring and Finding generation
sub_phases.objective: Compute a deterministic review-depth score per PR and generate the first Finding records.

tasks.title: Implement review-depth scoring logic
tasks.objective: Compute a score from available PR metadata: time from open to merge, comment count, number of distinct reviewers, per blueprint Section 6/7's description of this as a comprehension proxy.
tasks.detailed_description: This must be explicitly documented in the product (per blueprint Section 15) as a proxy, not a certainty - the scoring function itself should be simple, explainable, and versioned so it can be tuned later without ambiguity about what changed.
inputs: PullRequest metadata already ingested in PHASE-2
expected_outputs: A documented, versioned scoring function producing a review-depth value per PR
tasks.implementation_notes: Keep the scoring function pure/deterministic and unit-testable in isolation from the database.
tasks.validation: Unit tests cover a range of realistic PR metadata inputs and expected score outputs.
failure_cases: Missing metadata (e.g., no reviewer recorded) -> defined fallback behavior, not a crash
tasks.security_considerations: Not applicable - pure computation on already-ingested, tenant-scoped data.
testing_requirements: Unit tests covering normal, missing-data, and edge-case PR metadata
definition_of_done: Scoring function implemented, versioned, and unit-tested

tasks.title: Generate Finding records from scored, tagged PRs
tasks.objective: Create the Finding entity per blueprint Section 16, populated with review-depth score and criticality tag, triggered on new PR ingestion (webhook) and during backfill.
tasks.detailed_description: A Finding is created or updated (not duplicated) per PR, referencing the PR and carrying status (open by default), review-depth score, and criticality tag. AI-authorship-confidence field exists in the schema now but remains null/unset until PHASE-4.
expected_outputs: Finding records correctly created for all ingested PRs, including the backfilled history
affected_components: Ingestion module (trigger point on new webhook events)
tasks.implementation_notes: Must handle the existing backfilled PR data from PHASE-2 as well as new incoming PRs via webhook - both paths converge on the same Finding-generation logic, not duplicated code paths.
tasks.validation: Findings correctly generated for both a backfilled repo and a newly-arriving webhook PR event, with correct tenant scoping.
failure_cases: PR updated after initial Finding creation (e.g., more commits pushed) -> Finding is updated, not duplicated, keyed on the PR's unique identifier
tasks.security_considerations: Tenant isolation on Finding records verified with the same adversarial-test discipline as PHASE-2.4.
testing_requirements: Integration test for Finding generation on backfill
Integration test for Finding generation/update on webhook event
Adversarial tenant-isolation test on Finding records
definition_of_done: Findings correctly and securely generated for all ingested PR data, old and new

expected_artifacts: Populated Finding data for a real test repo
sub_phases.testing_strategy: Unit tests for scoring, integration tests for Finding generation on both backfill and webhook paths, adversarial tenant-isolation test.
security_checks: Tenant isolation on Finding records verified
validation_steps: Manual spot-check of generated Findings against real PR data for plausibility
completion_criteria: Findings correctly generated, scored, and tagged for a real connected repository
sub_phases.rollback_considerations: Additive schema; scoring logic is versioned so future tuning does not silently reinterpret historical Findings without an explicit migration/recompute decision.
risks: Review-depth score being a weak proxy for actual comprehension is an acknowledged, inherent limitation (per blueprint's own honesty about this) - mitigated by clear UI framing in PHASE-5, not by pretending the proxy is more certain than it is

phase_validation.method: Manual review of generated Findings against real repository data for plausibility, plus full adversarial tenant-isolation suite passing.
phase_validation.gate: Product Gate (partial) - the deterministic half of the core value proposition is now demonstrable, even without AI.

definition_of_done: Org Admin can configure criticality policy
Findings are correctly generated with review-depth score and criticality tag for both backfilled and new PRs
Tenant isolation verified on all new entities
AI-authorship field exists in schema but is correctly deferred to PHASE-4, not stubbed with fake data

phases.name: AI-Authorship Classification and AI Orchestration Layer
phases.objective: Resolve the blueprint's single largest identified technical risk: implement AI-authorship classification behind a robust orchestration layer with schema validation, provider fallback, and cost controls.
phases.business_reason: This is the differentiating half of the product's core value; the blueprint explicitly flags it as the highest-severity, highest-probability technical risk and requires it be de-risked deliberately, not rushed.
phases.technical_reason: Implements the AI Orchestration Service, structured-output validation, and provider fallback per blueprint Sections 8, 9, 10, and 15.
phases.expected_outcome: Findings carry an AI-assessed authorship-confidence value, clearly badged as AI-derived per blueprint Section 4's trust-badge requirement, with validated, bounded, cost-controlled AI usage.

prerequisite_tasks: Pre-flight item PF-2 (AI provider selection) resolved as a blocking prerequisite task within this phase
external_dependencies: Verified AI provider data-retention/training terms adequate for source-code processing - explicitly required before any real (non-synthetic) code is sent
required_credentials_access: Human developer must create AI provider account(s) and confirm current terms of service/data handling policy for the account tier used

included: AI Orchestration Service with structured-output/schema validation
Secrets pre-filtering before any AI call (per blueprint Section 9 data-flow rule)
Cost controls and per-org rate limiting on AI calls
Curated evaluation dataset for regression testing (blueprint Section 15)
excluded: Comprehension-challenge feature (uses this infrastructure but is built in PHASE-6, per blueprint Section 22's explicit dependency ordering)
affected_users: Indirectly all users, via the Findings they view; no new direct UI in this phase beyond surfacing the AI badge, which is PHASE-5

sub_phases.name: AI provider selection and data-handling verification
sub_phases.objective: Resolve PF-2 with a documented, verified decision before any real code is sent to any AI provider.

tasks.title: Verify current AI provider data-retention/training terms
tasks.objective: Confirm, from current provider documentation, whether the selected provider's relevant account tier offers a no-training/appropriate-retention guarantee for API-submitted data, per blueprint Section 8's explicit requirement.
tasks.detailed_description: This must be checked against live, current documentation at implementation time, not assumed from the earlier blueprint discussion, which itself flagged this as unverified.
expected_outputs: Documented verification record: provider, account tier, confirmed data-handling terms, source checked
tasks.implementation_notes: If verification cannot be completed with confidence, this must be explicitly reported as unresolved rather than proceeding on an assumption - this task blocks all subsequent AI-related work in this phase until resolved.
tasks.validation: Documented verification reviewed and approved by human developer before proceeding.
failure_cases: No provider can be verified to have adequate terms at reasonable cost -> escalate to human developer for a business decision, not silently proceed with an unverified provider
tasks.security_considerations: This task exists specifically to prevent the data-leakage risk identified in blueprint Section 10.
definition_of_done: Verification record documented and human-approved

tasks.title: Select and configure primary and fallback AI providers
tasks.objective: Finalize primary and secondary provider selection per blueprint Section 8's explicit fallback requirement.
expected_outputs: Provider API credentials configured as secrets
Basic connectivity test to both providers succeeding
tasks.implementation_notes: Fallback provider must also pass the same T-4.1.1 verification standard, not be added as an afterthought with lower scrutiny.
tasks.validation: Successful test call to both primary and fallback providers using non-sensitive synthetic test data only at this stage.
failure_cases: Fallback provider's terms are inadequate -> either find an adequate alternative or explicitly document graceful-degradation-only fallback behavior with human sign-off
tasks.security_considerations: API keys stored via the secrets mechanism established in PHASE-1, never hardcoded.
testing_requirements: Connectivity test to both providers using synthetic, non-sensitive data
definition_of_done: Both providers configured, verified, and connectivity-tested with synthetic data

expected_artifacts: Documented provider verification and selection record
sub_phases.testing_strategy: Connectivity tests with synthetic data only.
security_checks: No real customer code sent to any provider until verification is complete and approved
validation_steps: Human developer sign-off on the verification record
completion_criteria: Verified, approved primary and fallback providers configured
sub_phases.rollback_considerations: Provider choice is behind an abstraction (AI Orchestration Service) specifically so it can be changed later without touching calling code, per blueprint Section 8's architectural intent.
risks: This is a hard blocking gate specifically because sending real source code to an unverified provider would violate the product's own core trust proposition - treated with maximum seriousness, not routine

sub_phases.name: AI Orchestration Service with structured output and validation
sub_phases.objective: Build the isolated service layer through which all AI calls are made, enforcing schema validation and scoped, minimal data sending, per blueprint Sections 8, 9, and 15.

tasks.title: Implement secrets pre-filtering on outbound diff content
tasks.objective: Detect and strip likely secrets/credentials from any code snippet before it is included in an AI call, per blueprint Section 9's explicit required-safety-step.
tasks.detailed_description: Use a pattern-based secrets-detection pass (common credential/key patterns) as a pre-filter; this is a safety net, not a claim of perfect detection, and must be documented as such.
inputs: Raw diff/snippet content destined for an AI call
expected_outputs: Filtered content with detected secret-like patterns redacted before any external call
tasks.implementation_notes: This filter runs on every single outbound snippet, with no code path that bypasses it - enforced structurally, not by convention.
tasks.validation: Unit tests with known secret-pattern examples confirm redaction; test that non-secret code is not falsely mangled beyond acceptable bounds.
failure_cases: Pattern-based detection misses a real secret -> documented as a known limitation, not claimed as complete protection
tasks.security_considerations: This task directly implements blueprint Section 9's 'must never be sent' data-classification rule for secrets.
testing_requirements: Unit tests covering common secret patterns
Test confirming normal code is not corrupted by the filter
definition_of_done: Pre-filter implemented, tested, and structurally unbypassable

tasks.title: Implement scoped-context enforcement
tasks.objective: Ensure only the specific diff/function relevant to a given analysis is sent, never the full repository or unrelated files, per blueprint Section 9.
tasks.detailed_description: The orchestration layer's function signature should make it structurally difficult to accidentally pass more context than intended - e.g., accept a bounded snippet type, not an arbitrary file/repo reference.
expected_outputs: AI calls provably scoped to only the relevant diff
tasks.implementation_notes: Design the internal API to make over-scoping a type error where feasible, not just a documentation convention.
tasks.validation: Test confirming a call cannot be constructed with more than the intended scope without an explicit, deliberate code change.
failure_cases: Not applicable - this is a structural constraint, not a runtime failure mode
tasks.security_considerations: Directly implements the data-minimization principle from blueprint Section 9.
testing_requirements: Test/type-check confirming scoping constraint
definition_of_done: Scoping constraint structurally enforced and tested

tasks.title: Implement structured-output schema validation for AI-authorship classification
tasks.objective: Every AI classification call must return output conforming to a strict schema; malformed output is rejected, never rendered, per blueprint Section 15.
tasks.detailed_description: Use the provider's function-calling/JSON-schema mode (per blueprint Section 8) rather than free-text parsing. On validation failure: retry once, then fall back to an explicit 'AI assessment unavailable' state, per blueprint Section 14.
expected_outputs: Validated authorship-confidence result, or an explicit unavailable state - never raw/unvalidated output
tasks.implementation_notes: Schema validation must happen server-side regardless of the provider's own claimed structured-output guarantees - defense in depth per blueprint Section 15.
tasks.validation: Test with a deliberately malformed provider response (simulated) to confirm rejection and fallback behavior.
failure_cases: Provider returns malformed output -> rejected, retried once, then falls back to unavailable state, logged
Provider call times out -> same fallback path
tasks.security_considerations: Prevents any AI hallucination from being silently trusted as fact, per blueprint's core AI-reliability principle.
testing_requirements: Test valid structured response accepted
Test malformed response rejected with correct fallback
Test timeout handled with correct fallback
definition_of_done: Structured-output validation implemented and tested for all listed cases

tasks.title: Implement provider fallback on primary failure
tasks.objective: Automatically retry a failed/unavailable primary-provider call against the verified fallback provider, per blueprint Section 8.
expected_outputs: Successful fallback-provider result, or the documented unavailable state if both fail
tasks.implementation_notes: Fallback attempt must go through the same schema-validation path as the primary - no relaxed validation for the fallback provider.
tasks.validation: Test simulating primary provider failure confirms fallback is attempted and, if it succeeds, produces a correctly validated result.
failure_cases: Both providers fail -> explicit unavailable state, not a crash or silent gap
tasks.security_considerations: Not applicable beyond what T-4.2.3 already covers.
testing_requirements: Test primary-failure-triggers-fallback path
Test both-fail path
definition_of_done: Fallback mechanism implemented and tested

tasks.title: Implement per-org cost controls and rate limiting on AI calls
tasks.objective: Prevent runaway AI spend per blueprint Section 8's explicit cost-control requirement.
tasks.detailed_description: Cache classification results per diff (a given diff does not need re-classification, per blueprint Section 8) and enforce a configurable monthly cost/call ceiling per Organization, with alerting before the limit is hit.
expected_outputs: Caching layer preventing redundant calls
Enforced per-org ceiling with pre-limit alerting
tasks.implementation_notes: Ceiling values are a configuration/business decision, not an engineering invention - flagged as requiring human/business input on actual limit values, though the mechanism itself is an engineering task.
tasks.validation: Test confirming a cached diff does not trigger a second AI call; test confirming ceiling enforcement blocks further calls once reached, with a clear user-facing message, not a silent failure.
failure_cases: Ceiling reached mid-backfill -> remaining Findings correctly marked 'AI assessment pending, quota reached' rather than silently skipped without explanation
tasks.security_considerations: Prevents a compromised/misbehaving integration from causing unbounded cost exposure.
testing_requirements: Test caching prevents duplicate calls
Test ceiling enforcement and correct user-facing state
definition_of_done: Caching and cost-ceiling enforcement implemented and tested

expected_artifacts: Populated authorship-confidence data on real Findings (using verified-adequate provider terms)
sub_phases.testing_strategy: Extensive unit and integration testing per task, given this sub-phase carries the project's single highest-severity technical risk.
security_checks: Secrets pre-filtering verified
Scoped-context enforcement verified
Schema validation verified against malformed input
No cross-tenant data mixing in any AI call, verified
validation_steps: Manual review of real classification results on the test repository for plausibility
completion_criteria: AI Orchestration Service fully implemented, tested, and producing plausible, safely-bounded results on a real test repository
sub_phases.rollback_considerations: Provider abstraction allows switching providers without touching calling code, mitigating lock-in risk.
risks: Classification accuracy itself (as opposed to the orchestration plumbing around it) remains the project's largest unresolved risk - this sub-phase makes the plumbing trustworthy but does not by itself prove the classifier's real-world accuracy, which requires PHASE-4.3's evaluation dataset work

sub_phases.name: Evaluation dataset and regression testing
sub_phases.objective: Build the curated, human-labeled evaluation set required by blueprint Section 15 before trusting the classifier's output in any user-facing way.

tasks.title: Curate labeled evaluation dataset
tasks.objective: Assemble a set of real PRs with human-assigned ground-truth labels (AI-authored: yes/no/uncertain, with rationale) to measure classifier accuracy against, per blueprint Section 15.
tasks.detailed_description: Sourced from the PHASE-0 manual-analysis work if suitable data exists there, plus additional labeling as needed. This is a human-labor task requiring human judgment, not something the IDE can generate on its own.
inputs: Real PR data from test/pilot repositories, with permission
expected_outputs: A versioned evaluation dataset of realistic size (exact size to be determined by available labeled data - not fabricated)
affected_components: New evaluation-dataset storage (could be a simple versioned file/table, not necessarily a complex system)
tasks.implementation_notes: Dataset size and composition depends entirely on data actually available and human labeling capacity - this must not be invented or padded to look more rigorous than it is.
tasks.validation: Dataset reviewed by human developer for label quality/consistency before use.
failure_cases: Insufficient labeled data available -> explicitly document the resulting reduced confidence in classifier validation, do not proceed as if a robust eval set exists when it does not
tasks.security_considerations: Same data-handling discipline as any other real customer code applies to this dataset.
tasks.testing_requirements: Not applicable - this produces test fixtures, not code under test itself.
definition_of_done: Evaluation dataset exists, versioned, human-reviewed for quality

tasks.title: Implement automated regression testing against the evaluation dataset
tasks.objective: Run the classifier against the evaluation dataset automatically on every prompt or model change, per blueprint Section 15's explicit requirement.
tasks.detailed_description: Report accuracy/precision/recall-style metrics (exact metric choice appropriate to a classification task) and flag any regression versus the previous baseline.
expected_outputs: Automated eval run producing a scored report, integrated into CI for any change touching the AI Orchestration module's prompts
tasks.implementation_notes: This becomes a required, non-skippable CI check for any future change to the classification prompt/logic, per blueprint Section 22's explicit dependency note that comprehension-grading work in PHASE-6 must not begin without this infrastructure in place.
tasks.validation: Eval run executes successfully and produces a baseline score against the current classifier version.
failure_cases: Eval run itself fails to execute (infra issue) -> must be fixed before proceeding, cannot be skipped
tasks.security_considerations: Not applicable beyond standard CI secret handling.
tasks.testing_requirements: The eval run is itself the test mechanism for this task.
definition_of_done: Automated eval integrated into CI, baseline score recorded

expected_artifacts: Automated CI eval check with a recorded baseline score
sub_phases.testing_strategy: The evaluation run itself; this sub-phase is testing infrastructure for the AI feature.
security_checks: Data-handling discipline applied to the evaluation dataset itself
validation_steps: Baseline eval score recorded and reviewed by human developer
completion_criteria: Evaluation dataset and automated regression check exist and produce a documented baseline accuracy figure - whatever that figure honestly turns out to be
sub_phases.rollback_considerations: not_applicable - test infrastructure
risks: If the baseline accuracy is poor, this is critical information that must directly inform whether PHASE-5 onward proceeds as planned or requires a scope reconsideration - explicitly not something to proceed past silently

phase_validation.method: Review of the documented baseline classifier accuracy against the evaluation dataset; review of all security checks in PHASE-4.2.
phase_validation.gate: Security Gate (AI-specific portion) and a critical checkpoint against the blueprint's #1-ranked technical risk.

definition_of_done: AI provider(s) selected with verified, adequate data-handling terms
AI Orchestration Service enforces secrets pre-filtering, scoped context, structured-output validation, and provider fallback
Cost controls and rate limiting implemented
Evaluation dataset exists with a documented, honest baseline accuracy score
Human developer has explicitly reviewed the baseline accuracy and decided whether to proceed, pause, or adjust scope before PHASE-5

phases.name: Core UX: Dashboard, Progressive Disclosure, and Reporting
phases.objective: Build the primary user-facing experience: the dashboard, the four-layer progressive-disclosure Finding detail page, and basic report export.

sub_phases.name: Finding detail page - full progressive disclosure
sub_phases.objective: Implement the exact 4-layer disclosure pattern from blueprint Section 4 - the single most important UX element in the product.

tasks.title: Implement Layer 1 (simple) and Layer 2 (explanation)
tasks.objective: Render the plain-language summary and explanation for a Finding, generated from the deterministic and AI-assessed data already computed in Phases 3-4.
tasks.detailed_description: Per blueprint Section 4's exact example pattern - Layer 1 states what happened, Layer 2 explains why it matters, using the Finding's criticality tag, review-depth score, and authorship confidence to construct the sentence. This text generation is templated/deterministic based on the underlying data, not a fresh AI call per view (avoiding unnecessary AI cost/latency for what is fundamentally a data-driven sentence).
inputs: Finding record with all Phase 3/4 fields populated
expected_outputs: Layer 1/2 text rendering correctly for a range of real Finding examples
tasks.implementation_notes: Templated text generation, not a live LLM call - keeps this fast, cheap, and deterministic, appropriate since the underlying data is already computed.
tasks.validation: Manual review of generated text against a range of real Findings for clarity and accuracy.
failure_cases: Missing/null authorship-confidence (e.g., AI assessment still pending) -> template correctly reflects 'pending' state, not a broken sentence
tasks.security_considerations: Not applicable - reads already-validated data.
testing_requirements: Unit tests for the templating logic covering normal, pending-AI-assessment, and edge-case data combinations
definition_of_done: Layer 1/2 rendering correctly and clearly across tested scenarios

cross_phase_requirements.tenant_isolation_testing: An adversarial tenant-isolation test is required for every new data-bearing entity introduced in any phase, not just once - this is a standing requirement, not a single checklist item.
cross_phase_requirements.audit_logging: Every state-changing action introduced from PHASE-5.3 onward must write an AuditLog entry - established as a pattern, applied consistently in every later phase.
cross_phase_requirements.ai_output_validation: No AI-derived value may be persisted or displayed without passing structured-output schema validation, per PHASE-4.2, in every phase that touches AI output including PHASE-6's comprehension-check feature.
cross_phase_requirements.cost_verification: Any external service's pricing/free-tier terms must be verified live at the time of integration in every phase that adds a new external dependency, per global_rules - never carried forward as an assumption from an earlier phase's research.
cross_phase_requirements.backend_language_decision: Resolved in PHASE-1.1; binding for all subsequent phases unless an explicit, human-approved architectural change is recorded.
cross_phase_requirements.ai_provider_decision: Resolved in PHASE-4.1; binding for all subsequent phases unless an explicit, human-approved change is recorded, including for PHASE-6's comprehension-check feature which reuses this same provider selection.

risk_register.description: AI-authorship classification accuracy is insufficient to be credible to users.
risk_register.detection_method: PHASE-4.3 evaluation dataset baseline score; PHASE-0 manual analysis reaction log as an early leading indicator.
risk_register.mitigation: Structural: confidence indicators shown in UI (never presented as certain), deterministic cross-checks preferred over pure AI inference where possible, explicit 'AI-assessed' badging throughout per PHASE-5.1.
risk_register.contingency: If baseline accuracy is poor, human developer decision required at the PHASE-4 gate on whether to narrow scope (e.g., rely more heavily on tool-metadata signals where available, reduce reliance on pure code-pattern inference) before proceeding to PHASE-5.
risk_register.owner: human_developer, informed by planning_and_review_layer's technical assessment
risk_register.status: open, being actively de-risked in PHASE-4

risk_register.description: No confirmed paying buyer or resolved buyer persona.
risk_register.mitigation: PHASE-0 is structured as a hard blocking gate specifically to surface this before deep engineering investment.
risk_register.contingency: Documented pivot-or-stop decision required at PHASE-0.3 if evidence is weak; human developer retains authority to consciously accept the risk and proceed anyway, but must do so explicitly, not by default.

risk_register.description: Selected AI provider's data-handling terms prove inadequate for source-code processing, late in the build.
risk_register.mitigation: Provider abstraction (AI Orchestration Service) designed specifically so provider changes do not require rewriting calling code.
risk_register.contingency: If no provider verifies adequately at reasonable cost, escalate to human developer for a business decision before any real customer code is processed.
risk_register.owner: human_developer for the business decision; planning_and_review_layer for technical verification support

risk_register.description: Tenant-isolation bug allows cross-organization data leakage.
risk_register.detection_method: Mandatory adversarial tenant-isolation test on every new data-bearing entity, per cross_phase_requirements.
risk_register.mitigation: Defense in depth: application-layer scoping plus Postgres Row-Level Security, per blueprint Section 10.
risk_register.contingency: Any failure of a tenant-isolation test blocks the phase from being marked done, no exceptions.
risk_register.owner: planning_and_review_layer to enforce the testing requirement; AI coding IDE to implement correctly
risk_register.status: open, standing mitigation in place from PHASE-1.5 onward

risk_register.description: GitHub API rate limits or webhook behavior differ from what was assumed at planning time.
risk_register.mitigation: Backoff/retry logic built into ingestion from PHASE-2.1 onward, not assumed unnecessary.
risk_register.contingency: Adjust backfill chunking/pacing based on real observed limits during PHASE-2.3 testing.
risk_register.owner: AI coding IDE to implement and report actual observed behavior; planning_and_review_layer to adjust plan if materially different from assumptions

risk_register.description: A well-funded incumbent (e.g., GitHub itself, or an existing AppSec vendor) launches a comparable accountability-focused feature during our build.
risk_register.detection_method: Not formally monitored within this engineering plan - a human developer market-awareness responsibility outside the scope of the phases above.
risk_register.mitigation: Speed to a validated, working V1 (this plan's phased approach) plus the fact that this framing is currently a genuine whitespace, per the earlier market research.
risk_register.contingency: Would require a human developer strategic reassessment, not an engineering response.
risk_register.status: open, monitored qualitatively, not blocking current phases
